evidence.clarity: At 1440 and 390, the headline, native range and play control convey a lamp that gradually lights the room before a set wake time.
evidence.fit: The site loads locally with no backend; the reservation copy correctly says no card is taken and explains that the action opens email.
evidence.distinctiveness: The SVG light scene is tied to the product, and the range input provides native keyboard and touch behavior.
evidence.proof: The range endpoints update the image/readout from Off at -30 to Full brightness at 0; probe reports no runtime errors or overflow.
evidence.craft: The 50KB single HTML contains SVG, semantic sections, form-like range control, CSS and JS; axe reports no issues, but CSS/JS are embedded together.
evidence.mobile: 390/320 have no overflow and text bottoms at 13px; the menu opens on phone, and the SVG/range stack without clipping.
evidence.honesty: The page labels its image as drawn and the light colors as illustrative; its final mailto destination is not present in the brief.
evidence.interaction: At all widths, range min/max and Play/Pause work; Escape closes the open mobile menu. There is no email form, so email edge-input tests do not apply.
evidence.copy: The controls are native and named, and the animation has a reduced-motion path; the page has no network-dependent code.
evidence.first_screen: At 1440 the scene, dial and reservation action are in the opening view; at 390 the action appears, but the readout is lower.

problems: The reserve CTA eventually uses an email destination absent from the brief.
All design and behavior live in one large HTML file, including the SVG scene and script.
The mobile illustration and its dial extend beyond the first viewport, so the full motion proof needs scrolling.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The repeated “Reserve a Morrow” action ultimately opens `mailto:reserve@morrow.example`, an address that the client brief does not supply.
hard_fail_flags.steps: At 390 or 1440, click the hero “Reserve a Morrow” anchor, then click the button in the reserve section. It resolves to `mailto:reserve@morrow.example`; the X08 brief provides no reservation email address.

evidence.clarity: The headline/lede state the bedside-lamp purpose and gradual dawn effect; the reserve form is the only way to express interest.
evidence.fit: The page honors the no-checkout-yet constraint about payment, but its local-only list state is not disclosed and cannot email the buyer.
evidence.distinctiveness: The custom dial is an accessible product-specific artifact, though the page is one inline HTML/CSS/JS file.
evidence.proof: End/Home and Play/Pause visibly change time/light; probe shows no overflow or errors at 390/320, but the form’s confirmation is not backed by a service.
evidence.craft: The custom slider has keyboard control and focus indication, the email is labeled, and axe reports no violations; HTML/CSS/JS are bundled in one file.
evidence.mobile: At 390 no horizontal overflow occurs, but the header has no phone menu and the reservation form sits far below the interactive scene.
evidence.honesty: The “place is held” confirmation and promise of emails are false in this delivered page: HOLD_ENDPOINT is empty and only localStorage changes.
evidence.interaction: Empty, zero, negative and malformed emails show a nearby error; a 2,000-character syntactically valid value is accepted, paste succeeds, and undo removes the saved value.
evidence.copy: “No account, no app” and “hardware runs late” are concrete; the success microcopy overstates what has happened.
evidence.first_screen: 1440 shows the simulator beside the promise; at 390 the signup action is absent from the opening view.

problems: The confirmation promises a queue place and future email without transmitting or persisting beyond localStorage.
Valid email lengths have no upper bound, and success focus moves into the confirmation without stating the device-only storage.
The long mobile hero delays the form and uses an always-visible nav instead of a compact menu.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: After a valid email, the page announces “Your place is held” and promises future emails, but the script only writes the value to localStorage; `HOLD_ENDPOINT` is empty and no request or backend receives it.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open B/index.html, scroll to Reserve, submit a valid email, then inspect the confirmation and `localStorage.morrow.held`. The form hides and promises future mail while no network submission occurs; reload in a fresh browser context and the place is gone.

reason: A uses a native range and handles reduced motion, while B has a more elaborate keyboard-capable dial and an undo path. B’s form nevertheless promises a server-side reservation without making a request, so I would favor A despite its monolithic file; an explicit local-only result or a real backend would change the decision.
